LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 6 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: when uttering questions and statements, 1. Why do we vary our voice when asking questions? 2. How does good pronunciation of words and sounds help us?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify correct stress and intonation in ‘WH’ questions, other questions and statements for clarity in speech,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. use correct stress and intonation in questions and statements to communicate clearly,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use vocabulary related to the theme in a variety of contexts for effective oral communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. adopt the use of varying intonation for effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify correct stress and intonation in ‘WH’ questions, other questions and statements for clarity in speech,

   Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. use correct stress and intonation in questions and statements to communicate clearly,

   Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. use vocabulary related to the theme in a variety of contexts for effective oral communication,

   Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. adopt the use of varying intonation for effective communication.

   Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an audio-visual recording of words featuring the sounds /ʊ/ /uː/ /f/ /v/

2. listen to correct stress in words such as address, increase among others (whether noun or verb),

3. listen to correct intonation in questions and statements to identify a speaker’s feelings,

4. recite a poem featuring ‘WH’ questions and declaratives collaboratively,

5. vary intonation

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an audio-visual recording of words featuring the sounds /ʊ/ /uː/ /f/ /v/
2. listen to correct stress in words such as address, increase among others (whether noun or verb),
3. listen to correct intonation in questions and statements to identify a speaker’s feelings,
4. recite a poem featuring ‘WH’ questions and declaratives collaboratively,
5. vary intonation

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner is able to recite poems collaboratively.

• Self-efficacy: This is developed as the learner achieves correct stress and intonation in speech.

Values:
● Responsibility: This is enhanced as the learner is able to take initiative of creating sentences using vocabulary

individually.

● Love: It is promoted as the learner is able to show care as they assist peers to use correct stress and intonation in

sentences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Digital Literacy: This is promoted as the learner is able to use and manipulate digital devices to learn correct stress and

intonation.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to connect the concept of articulation with the learning in Kiswahili and Music.

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify correct stress and intonation in ‘WH’ questions, other questions and statements for clarity in speech,
2. use correct stress and intonation in questions and statements to communicate clearly,
3. use vocabulary related to the theme in a variety of contexts for effective oral communication,
4. adopt the use of varying intonation for effective communication.

Remember the key question: when uttering questions and statements, 1. Why do we vary our voice when asking questions? 2. How does good pronunciation of words and sounds help us?
